subject: Materials Science
title: Alloy Design for Corrosion Resistance
description: A short lesson to help you apply Alloy Design for Corrosion Resistance.

hook.text: Add 10.5% chromium to steel and it becomes stainless — a single alloying element transforms its corrosion behavior.

buildup.text: Chromium, nickel, and molybdenum each contribute to the passive film's stability and repair speed.

discovery.text: Molybdenum specifically improves pitting resistance — that's why 316 steel (with Mo) beats 304 in chlorides.

twist.text: Higher alloy content costs more and can reduce weldability — every improvement has a trade-off.

climax.text: Super duplex stainless steels handle offshore oil production — resisting chlorides, hydrogen sulfide, and high pressure.

punchline.text: The right alloy recipe makes corrosion a problem someone else has.

quiz.question: What role does molybdenum play in stainless steel?
options: It improves resistance to pitting corrosion
